lilly_hyleg_alcocoden_and_years.location: Book III, Chapter CIV, printed pp. 527-531; Mercury's planetary years, printed p. 80
lilly_hyleg_alcocoden_and_years.verified_summary: Lilly selects the sect light when it occupies an eligible hylegical place, rejects the eighth and twelfth for the luminaries, and otherwise proceeds through the alternate light, prenatal lunation rulers, and Ascendant. The Arabic Alcocoden is the planet with essential dignity at the Hyleg that beholds it; Lilly also records a preference for superior essential dignity when no contender aspects. An angular, strong, fortunate Alcocoden may give its greater years. Lilly's table assigns Mercury 76 greater years, 48 mean years, and 20 least years.
lilly_hyleg_alcocoden_and_years.publication_limit: Lilly says the native might live the selected years only if no obstructive directions, sudden casualties, or general calamity intervene. In the same chapter he explicitly says he is not satisfied that the Hyleg, Anareta, or Alcocoden can yet be selected with certainty and calls for verification from completed lives. Publish the exact branch result and competing branch, never a single guaranteed death age.

dorotheus_sect_light_triplicity_fortune.location: Carmen Astrologicum I.1, I.5, I.22 and I.23-24, read in Umar al-Tabari's ARABIC, Pingree Teubner 1976 (Arabic pp. 3-4, 6-8, 20-24). Pingree's English of the same material at printed pp. 161-162 and 183-189.
dorotheus_sect_light_triplicity_fortune.verified_summary: Read in Umar's Arabic. I.1 gives the triplicity table (verified systematically against DOROTHEAN_TRIPLICITY, all four elements). I.22 gives the judgment this rule encodes, in his own words: 'if the native is DIURNAL look to the SUN and the lords of its triplicity, and if NOCTURNAL look to the MOON and the lords of its triplicity. If you find the FIRST and SECOND triplicity lords both together, or each separately, in a good place, his affair will not cease from the first year to the end of his life in excellence and elevation and abundance' - then the mixed cases, first good / second bad and first bad / second good, which is where the beginning-versus-later reading comes from. I.5 ranks the places by strength: Ascendant, Midheaven, 11th, 5th ('the house of the child'), 7th. Chapters 23-24 are Dorotheus's own WORKED EXAMPLES of the rule, drawn as square horoscope diagrams: a DIURNAL native whose first and second triplicity lords of the Sun (Sun, then Jupiter) both stand IN THE ANGLES and who prospers and is praised by kings and nobles; and a NOCTURNAL native whose first and second lords of the Moon's triplicity (Mercury, then Saturn) are both CADENT and below the earth, with the contrary result. The examples confirm the mechanism the engine implements - sect light, first and second lord, judged by placement - from Dorotheus's own demonstrations rather than by inference.
dorotheus_sect_light_triplicity_fortune.publication_limit: The TRIPLICITY TABLE is verified from the Arabic. Two things are not. (1) The Arabic at I.1 adds a clause the engine has no slot for: 'wa-fi al-sunbula aydan hazzun li-utarid' - 'and in Virgo, Mercury too has a share'. That is a SIGN-SPECIFIC fourth participant inside the earth triplicity, and DOROTHEAN_TRIPLICITY is keyed by element, so no Virgo chart can express it. Recorded as a real gap, deliberately not patched into dignity scoring without deciding what weight a 'share' (hazz) carries - guessing that weight would silently move every Virgo chart's dignity totals. (2) Chapters 5 and 22-24, which this rule also cites for fortune and elevation, were read only in Pingree's English.

valens_decennials_129_months.location: Anthologiae VI.5-6, printed pp. 251-254 (Kroll 1908) - Valens proper. The same technique also appears at Kroll 367-372, but those pages fall inside the Additamenta vetusta (363-372), a later scribal appendix whose own Valentinian nativity (b. 419 CE) dates it three centuries after Valens.
valens_decennials_129_months.verified_summary: The major decennial period is 129 months, or 10 years 9 months. The seven sub-period shares are Saturn 30 months, Jupiter 12, Mars 15, Sun 19, Venus 8, Mercury 20, and Moon 25, assigned in the chart's zodiacal planetary order from an eligible aphetic light or the planet following the Ascendant. The shares sum exactly to 129 months. Read in the Greek at VI.5-6: the subdivision ratio minor_years/129 reproduces six of the seven figures in Valens's own worked Saturn example to the day (Jupiter differs by ~3 days, a probable OCR slip on the numeral).
valens_decennials_129_months.publication_limit: Riley labels the detailed computational exposition a fifth-century addition, even though the addition says the method is also found in Valens. Publish this as a Valens-tradition transmission, not uncontested authorial wording. Customer dates use modern civil calendar months to preserve 10 years 9 months; do not replace the months with uninterrupted 30-day blocks or import the fourth-ruler reset from the separate lunar-quarter method.

ibn_ezra_triplicity_life_thirds.location: Book of Revolution section 4, English p. 375 with facing Hebrew p. 374; referencing the Book of Nativities
ibn_ezra_triplicity_life_thirds.verified_summary: Ibn Ezra explicitly says the triplicity rulers of the Sun's sign by day or the Moon's sign by night rule the native's years, divided into three parts, and that the active ruler's condition must be compared between nativity and annual revolution.
ibn_ezra_triplicity_life_thirds.publication_limit: This is a later medieval life-phase doctrine, not the wording of Dorotheus I.22. It supports first, middle, and last relative phases but does not itself supply numerical age boundaries. Keep it separate from the Lilly-scoped Hyleg and Alcocoden branches published elsewhere in the report.

ibn_ezra_annual_revolution_core.location: Book of Revolution sections 1, 4, 15, and 21, English pp. 373, 375, 385, and 389 with facing Hebrew
ibn_ezra_annual_revolution_core.verified_summary: Ibn Ezra defines the annual revolution as the moment the Sun returns to its natal degree and minute, instructs the reader to cast the return Ascendant and planets, compare the sect-light triplicity ruler between nativity and return, inspect the ruler of the return Ascendant, and subordinate the shorter-lived annual indications to stronger natal and directional testimony.
ibn_ezra_annual_revolution_core.publication_limit: Do not mix Tajika Muntha, arbitrary point weights, or a modern Morin handover into this source-scoped method. Return houses are location-dependent; if the native's location at the return is unknown, disclose the use of natal coordinates as a proxy. The return modifies and times natal testimony rather than replacing it.

firmicus_antiscia_major_configurations.location: Matheseos II.29, Kroll-Skutsch Teubner 1897, printed pp. 77-84 (vol. 1)
firmicus_antiscia_major_configurations.verified_summary: Read in the Latin at II.29. The axis is solstitial, six mutual pairs: Gemini/Cancer, Leo/Taurus, Virgo/Aries, Pisces/Libra, Aquarius/Scorpio, Sagittarius/Capricorn - all six verified against calculate_antiscia_points. Firmicus prints the Gemini/Cancer degree table in full (1->29, 2->28 ... 15->15 ... 29->1) and says it holds for every pair; all 29 mappings verified exactly against the formula (180 - lambda) % 360. He states the reciprocity outright: the degree a part receives from, it sends back to.
firmicus_antiscia_major_configurations.publication_limit: Two things to carry. (1) Firmicus II.29,4 excludes the 30th degree - no part sends its antiscion to the 30th and the 30th sends to none. Under a continuous formula that degree IS the sign boundary (Gemini 30 = Cancer 0), so it is degenerate rather than mishandled, and is not special-cased; anyone diffing our output against his printed table at that one degree should know why. (2) Firmicus does not claim the doctrine: he names PTOLEMY as following no principle but antiscia, ANTIOCHUS as having touched it 'as if through a mirror' (the Libra-does-not-see-Aries remark is Antiochus's, not Ptolemy's), and DOROTHEUS OF SIDON as having explained it plainly in his FOURTH BOOK. Citing Firmicus here is nevertheless CORRECT and not second-best: Pingree prints this very passage as Carmen Astrologicum Appendix I, 'fr. 61 Stegemann', i.e. he classifies it as a FRAGMENT OF DOROTHEUS. An editor prints a testimonium because the primary text is lost - the antiscia chapter does not survive in the Arabic, so Firmicus IS the surviving witness for it.

picatrix_lunar_mansions_electional_scope.location: Ghayat al-Hakim, the lunar-mansion chapter, Ritter's Arabic, folios 19-22 (composite pages 398-401; folio = 420 - page, this scan binds right-to-left). Mansions 13-25 read directly; 1-12 and 26-28 lie on adjacent folios and are located but not yet read.
picatrix_lunar_mansions_electional_scope.verified_summary: Read in Ritter's Arabic. Each mansion is headed 'manzila' with its number and Arabic name - al-'Awwa' (13), al-Simak (14), al-Ghafr (15), al-Zubana (16), al-Iklil (17), al-Qalb (18), al-Shawla (19), al-Na'a'im (20), al-Balda (21), Sa'd al-Dhabih (22), Sa'd Bula' (23), Sa'd al-Su'ud (24), Sa'd al-Akhbiya (25) - and gives first its DEGREE SPAN ('wa-hiya min ... daraja ila ... daraja') and then its uses, introduced by 'yusna' fiha talsamat', 'in it are made talismans for'. The uses are ELECTIONAL and turn on the Moon being in the mansion: growth of trade and crops, the traveller's safety, release of prisoners, binding banners for kings, stability of building, and marriage - e.g. al-Iklil, 'they agree that whoever befriends a friend while the Moon is in this mansion, that friendship will not be severed'.
picatrix_lunar_mansions_electional_scope.publication_limit: SPLIT VERDICT after reading Ritter's Arabic. The BOUNDARIES are verified exact - equal 1/28 divisions of 12d51'26", agreeing with Ritter to the arc-second across mansions 1-12 and 26-28 - and Book I ch. 4 is the correct citation. The INTENTS are NOT verified and must not be presented as Picatrix: a 12-mansion comparison found a systematic, directional divergence, with the political and coercive operations removed (besieging cities, vengeance against kings, corrupting crops, binding and releasing prisoners) and benign domestic material added that has no Arabic counterpart (healing, childbirth, washing the body, new garments). Mansion 8 is inverted in sense. The likely origin is the second entry in each source_refs, a modern compilation cited as though co-equal with Picatrix. TWO SOURCE CONDITIONS ARE UNIMPLEMENTED. (1) The Moon gate, stated at both ends of the chapter and called al-'umda, the cardinal rule: perform no work until the Moon is in the degree agreeing with it; for works of GOOD the Moon must be pure of malefics and combustion and applying to a benefic, and for works of EVIL the reverse. A mansion does not simply mean its uses. (2) Picatrix credits the entire system to India and is reporting a foreign tradition, not asserting his own.

sect_malefic_moderation.location: Book I, chapter 7 (ζ΄. Περὶ ἡμερινῶν καὶ νυκτερινῶν), source file lines 2498-2522
sect_malefic_moderation.verified_summary: Saturn, being cooling, is assigned to the heat of the day, and Mars, being drying, to the moisture of the night, 'for thus each, obtaining proportion through the mixture, becomes proper to the sect that provides good temperament.' The mechanism Ptolemy names is TEMPERING by the opposite quality, not reward.
sect_malefic_moderation.publication_limit: In-sect moderates a malefic. It does not make the malefic a benefic, ally, or universal stabilizer. See ptolemy_sect_membership for the membership list from the same chapter.

ptolemaic_triplicity_rulers.location: Book I, chapter 19 (ιθ΄. Περὶ τριγώνων), source file lines 3748-3901
ptolemaic_triplicity_rulers.verified_summary: Fire: Sun by day, Jupiter by night, Mars expressly EXCLUDED on sect grounds though he owns Aries. Earth: Venus by day, Moon by night. Air: Saturn by day, Mercury by night. Water: 'it was left to Mars, he being the sole one remaining and having a relation to it through the house of Scorpio, and co-ruling it WITH HIM - on account of both the sect and the femininity of the signs - by night the Moon, and by day Venus.' Water is Ptolemy's only three-ruler triangle.
ptolemaic_triplicity_rulers.publication_limit: This settles the water-triplicity fork. Lilly's Mars-by-day-and-night reads only the first clause; the common Venus/Moon table reads only the second. Ptolemy says both in one sentence. Our PTOLEMAIC_TRIPLICITY water row (Venus, Moon) is the correct sect-split and Lilly's Mars is correctly held in a separate LILLY_TRIPLICITY table. KNOWN GAP: the two-slot structure cannot represent Mars as a ruler of the water triangle in both sects, which Ptolemy gives, so that dignity is currently unscored.

ptolemaic_terms.location: Book I, chapter 21 (κα΄. Περὶ ὁρίων διαθέσεως), source file lines 3986 ff. - chapter opening read; the bound table itself is NOT yet transcribed
ptolemaic_terms.verified_summary: Ptolemy names exactly two transmitted bound systems: the EGYPTIAN, which goes by the rulerships of the houses, and the CHALDEAN, which goes by the rulerships of the triangles. He then attacks the Egyptian bounds directly, arguing they preserve consistency neither of order nor of quantity, and gives six specific counterexamples (why Saturn first in Libra and not Venus; why Jupiter in Aries and not Mars; why Mercury first in Capricorn, having no rulership there at all). He also notes that the planets' bound-totals are what 'they say the time-periods are apportioned by', and is unconvinced.
ptolemaic_terms.publication_limit: Ptolemy does NOT call his own table Ptolemaic; that name is posthumous. Our PTOLEMAIC_TERMS_LILLY1647 table was keyed from photographs of Lilly's 1647 printing of Ptolemy's table, NOT from Ptolemy's Greek. Transcribing the Greek table (source file lines ~4100-4459) and checking ours against it is outstanding work.

ptolemaic_aspects.location: Book I, chapter 14 (ιδ΄. Περὶ τῶν συσχηματιζομένων δωδεκατημορίων), source file lines 3421-3494
ptolemaic_aspects.verified_summary: Ptolemy defines exactly four configurations - opposition (two right angles, six signs, 180 degrees), trine (one and a third right angles, four signs, 120 degrees), square (one right angle, three signs, 90 degrees) and sextile (two thirds of a right angle, two signs, 60 degrees). He calls trine and sextile CONCORDANT (symphonoi) and square and opposition DISCORDANT (asymphonoi), and gives the reason: concordant aspects join signs of the same gender, discordant ones join signs of opposite gender. The distinction is structural, not moral.
ptolemaic_aspects.publication_limit: The conjunction is NOT among Ptolemy's four configurations; synodos is treated separately. This passage verifies the aspect set, the geometry, and the concordant/discordant split with Ptolemy's own reason for it. It does not verify our numerical orb allowances or the applying/separating algorithm.

ptolemy_doryphory_rank.location: Apotelesmatika IV.3 (gamma', Peri tyches axiomatikes), Boll-Boer Teubner 1957, printed pp. 176-179; and III.5 (Peri goneon, the parents), which in this edition ENDS at printed p. 120 - p. 120 opens ch. 6 Peri adelphon. The previously recorded 'printed pp. 120-121' for the parents is another edition's pagination.
ptolemy_doryphory_rank.verified_summary: Ptolemy places attendants in the luminary's sign or the sign next following, especially morning or oriental stars with the Sun and evening or occidental stars with the Moon. Rank then depends on the luminaries' gender and angularity, the attendants' angular testimony, and the attendants' nature and condition. Read in the Greek at IV.3, p. 178: Saturn's attendance confers rank 'epi polyktemosyne kai synagoge chrematon kai dynasteias'; JUPITER OR VENUS - 'ho de tou Dios e ho tes Aphrodites', a SINGLE shared clause, not two - 'epi charisi kai doreais kai timais kai megalopsychia'; Mars 'epi strateliasiais kai nikais kai phobois ton hypotetagmenon'; Mercury 'dia synesin e paideian kai epimeleian kai oikonomian ton pragmaton'. III.5 also read: sect selects the significator PAIR - by day chiefly the Sun and Venus, by night Saturn and the Moon - and the paternal or maternal place of the sect is then set up 'hosper horoskopon', AS IF IT WERE AN ASCENDANT, with everything else judged as for a nativity.
ptolemy_doryphory_rank.publication_limit: Do not replace the sign-based placement with a fixed thirty-degree window. Attendance is not itself a guarantee of kingship: the royal branch requires angular and masculine luminaries plus a complete attendant retinue, while debilitated or adverse attendants give subordinate, dangerous, or unstable dignity. Ashmand's Placidus footnote discusses aspectual attendance separately; the current audited engine publishes the bodily Ptolemaic branch only. NOTE on a gap that was recorded and turns out not to exist: an earlier pass reported Jupiter's line in this list as lost to OCR. It was never lost. Ptolemy gives Jupiter and Venus ONE clause between them, joined by 'e' (or), so there is no separate Jupiter entry to recover. Any implementation that assigns Jupiter its own distinct rank-signification here is inventing one. NOT BUILT from III.5: the derived-ascendant treatment of the parental place. Ptolemy turns the parent's significator place into a chart in its own right; the engine has no such layer, and adding one would put a second chart inside every reading. Recorded for a decision. Also note the parents page range carried here (120-121) is foreign to Boll-Boer - cite the chapter.
ptolemy_doryphory_rank.edition_limit_note: STILL ON ASHMAND 1822, which is Ashmand's English of PROCLUS' PARAPHRASE - Ptolemy at two removes. The chapter behind this rule has NOT yet been read in the Boll-Boer Greek. Repoint to ptolemy_apotelesmatika_boll_boer_teubner once it has. Do not present this as a direct Ptolemy citation.

ptolemy_perseus_algol.location: Apotelesmatika I.9 (constellations north of the zodiac), Boll-Boer Teubner 1957, printed p. 28; and IV.9 (Peri thanatou poiotetos, the quality of death), printed pp. 201-204. NOT 'p. 30' and NOT 'Book III ch. IX, pp. 209-210' as previously recorded - in this edition p. 30 opens ch. 10 on the seasons, and pp. 209-210 are Book IV.10 on the ages and prorogations. Both old ranges are another edition's.
ptolemy_perseus_algol.verified_summary: Both halves read in the Greek. I.9, p. 28: 'Hoi de kata ton Persea to te tou Dios kai to tou Kronou; he de en te labe tes machairas systrophe to tou Areos kai to tou Hermou' - Perseus is Jupiter and Saturn, the cluster in the SWORD HILT is Mars and Mercury. IV.9, p. 203: at the GORGONEION TOU PERSEOS the native dies 'kephalizomenous e meleokopoumenous', beheaded or dismembered. The engine's summary of both was accurate.
ptolemy_perseus_algol.publication_limit: TWO DIFFERENT STARS under one rule id. I.9's subject is the cluster in the sword hilt (the Double Cluster); IV.9's is the Gorgoneion, the Gorgon's head, which is where Algol sits. The sword-hilt nature must never be quoted as a statement about Algol. AND THE CONDITION IS NOT OPTIONAL: Ptolemy gives the beheading outcome only inside a larger anaretic judgment - p. 204, it applies 'when the stars controlling the ANARETIC PLACES have fallen into the cadent places, especially when the Moon is present at, or square or opposite, those places'. Algol alone, without that configuration, licenses nothing. Publishing the decapitation image on a bare Algol contact would misrepresent the source.
ptolemy_perseus_algol.edition_limit_note: STILL ON ASHMAND 1822, which is Ashmand's English of PROCLUS' PARAPHRASE - Ptolemy at two removes. The chapter behind this rule has NOT yet been read in the Boll-Boer Greek. Repoint to ptolemy_apotelesmatika_boll_boer_teubner once it has. Do not present this as a direct Ptolemy citation.

ptolemy_prorogation_distributor.location: Apotelesmatika IV.10 (Divisions of Times), Boll-Boer Teubner 1957, printed pp. 204-213. Chapter 10 opens at p. 204, the seven ages of man run at pp. 206-208, the five prorogations and the distributor mechanics at pp. 209-210, and the book ends at p. 213. The range 'printed pp. 214-218' previously recorded here is another edition's pagination (probably Robbins' Loeb) and lands past the end of this book.
ptolemy_prorogation_distributor.verified_summary: Read in the Greek at IV.10, printed pp. 209-210. FIVE prorogations run in parallel, each answering a different class of question: the Lot of Fortune for property (ta tes kteseos), the Moon for the affections of the soul and cohabitations, the Sun for rank and reputation (ta kat' axian kai doxan), the Midheaven for the remaining conduct of life - actions, friendships, childbearing - and the Ascendant for the body and foreign travel. The years given to the interval degrees differ by prorogation: the ASCENDANT release uses the ASCENSIONAL times of the native's own climate, the MIDHEAVEN release the times of CULMINATIONS. Annual chronocrators are then taken by casting the years from birth forward one sign at a time FROM EACH prorogatory place, taking the domicile lord of the completed sign; months are cast the same way from the places that took the year's rulership.
ptolemy_prorogation_distributor.publication_limit: The current engine publishes only the Ascendant bound distributor through a configured one-degree-per-year zodiacal oblique-ascension method using Egyptian bounds. Bound changes are numerically solved within annual brackets, but its latitude-free aspect points, key, bound table, and ray dates remain configured choices, not a complete reproduction of every Ptolemaic prorogation. Do not label it a full Placidus semi-arc direction suite. CITATION CAUTION: the page range this rule carried (214-218) does not exist in the edition now on disk - Boll-Boer's Tetrabiblos ends at printed 213. Any future check against 'pp. 214-218' will land in the addendum or past the end of the book. Cite chapter, not page, when editions are mixed. A DOCTRINAL CONSTRAINT FROM THE GREEK, not previously recorded. Ptolemy states outright that because the five prorogations run independently, 'at the same times there will NOT be ONE benefic or malefic lord of them, since many CONTRARY events for the most part happen at the same times' - he instances losing a family member while receiving an inheritance, or falling ill while attaining rank. He adds that a uniformly fortunate or wretched period, where all or most prorogations meet benefics or all meet malefics, happens RARELY. Any reading that collapses the prorogations into a single verdict for a period, or that describes a year as simply good or simply bad, contradicts this chapter. The engine currently publishes only the Ascendant distributor, so it cannot yet express the parallelism - but it must not present that single thread as Ptolemy's whole judgment of a time.
ptolemy_prorogation_distributor.edition_limit_note: STILL ON ASHMAND 1822, which is Ashmand's English of PROCLUS' PARAPHRASE - Ptolemy at two removes. The chapter behind this rule has NOT yet been read in the Boll-Boer Greek. Repoint to ptolemy_apotelesmatika_boll_boer_teubner once it has. Do not present this as a direct Ptolemy citation.

lilly_reception.location: Christian Astrology, London 1647 first edition, printed p. 112 (Of Reception)
lilly_reception.verified_summary: Read in Lilly's own 1647 English. Reception is two significators each in the other's dignity. Reception by domicile he calls 'the strongest and best of all receptions'; it may also be by triplicity, term, face, or any essential dignity. Its stated use is to effect a matter that is otherwise denied.
lilly_reception.publication_limit: Reception is MUTUAL - both planets in each other's dignity. A one-way placement is not reception in Lilly's sense. He ranks domicile reception strongest but admits the minor dignities, so a term or face reception is real and weaker, not absent.

lilly_planetary_conditions.location: Christian Astrology, London 1647 first edition, printed p. 115, 'A ready Table whereby to examine the Fortitudes and Debilities of the Planets'
lilly_planetary_conditions.verified_summary: Lilly gives planetary natures, houses, exaltations, falls, triplicity rights, terms, and related conditions. Verified against the 1647 table: house 5, exaltation 4, triplicity 3, term 2, face 1, detriment -5, fall -4, peregrine -5. All eight match DignityCalculator exactly.
lilly_planetary_conditions.publication_limit: The exact page image controls when OCR glyphs obscure signs or planetary symbols. GAP: Lilly's table awards 'own house OR MUTUALL RECEPTION BY HOUSE' the same 5, and 'exaltation OR RECEPTION BY EXALTATION' the same 4. The engine implements neither - reception is computed in reception.py and never reaches the dignity score. The weight is explicit in the source so this is implementable without guessing, but it would change essential-dignity totals wherever a reception exists and the almuten is decided by those totals, so it is recorded for a deliberate decision rather than patched in passing.

lilly_degree_quality_tables.location: An Introduction to Astrology, Two necessary Tables of the Signes and The use of the Table, printed pp. 116-118
lilly_degree_quality_tables.verified_summary: Lilly tabulates masculine and feminine, light, dark, smoky, void, deep or pitted, lame or deficient, and increasing-fortune degrees. He applies light, dark, smoky, and void chiefly to the Ascendant and Moon; pitted degrees to the Ascendant, Moon, or Ascendant ruler; azimene degrees as corroboration through the Ascendant, Moon, Ascendant ruler, or principal lord when an existing bodily defect is already known; and increasing-fortune degrees to the second cusp or ruler, Jupiter, or Fortune.
lilly_degree_quality_tables.publication_limit: Do not apply a degree flag indiscriminately to every planet. The azimene passage is retrospective corroboration, not authority to predict a diagnosis or bodily defect from the flag alone. Masculine and feminine degrees answer sex questions and are not a general personality classification.

whole_sign_topical_chain.location: Paulus Alexandrinus, Eisagogika ch. 24, 'Peri tes ton dodeka topon pinakikes ektheseos', read in the BOER 1958 GREEK at printed p. 53. (The rule was registered against Schmidt's 1995 English, 'Chapter 24, On the Tabular Exposition of the Twelve Places, pp. 46-57'; that page range is Schmidt's and is correct for Schmidt.)
whole_sign_topical_chain.verified_summary: Read in the Greek at ch. 24, printed p. 53: 'Ton dodeka topon pros pasan apotelesmatographian lambanomenon ARCHE KAI PROTOSTASION ESTIN HO HOROSKOPOS' - of the twelve places, taken for every delineation, the BEGINNING and FIRST-STANDING is the Horoskopos, through which all matters pertaining to men are directed. That is the whole-sign chain the engine implements, in Paulus's own words.
whole_sign_topical_chain.publication_limit: The project's consolidated topic labels and ruler-condition heuristic draw on more than Paulus. Paulus verifies the whole-sign place framework only; the complete mapping remains a multi-author configured synthesis. paulus_planets_in_places_chart_rules.location: Chapter 24, On the Tabular Exposition of the Twelve Places, chart-relevant passages on printed pp. 46-57
paulus_planets_in_places_chart_rules.verified_summary: For the placements in the Fairfield test nativity, Paulus makes Hermes rejoice in the first; gives benefics in the fifth a child-producing promise; treats the eighth as inheritance and profit-from-death testimony even when occupied by malefics; gives Mars in the eleventh sharply different day and night outcomes; gives Venus in the eleventh favorable marriage and fortune unless afflicted by malefic rays; and supplies severe Sun and Moon delineations in the twelfth, with the Moon's harsher result conditioned on malefic regard or application.

paulus_dodecatemoria_x13.location: Eisagogika ch. 22 (κβ΄), Περὶ τῶν δωδεκατημορίων, Boer 1958 pp. 45-47
paulus_dodecatemoria_x13.verified_summary: Multiply the degree WITHIN its sign by 13 and distribute the product from the body's own sign at 30 degrees per sign. Worked example in the text: Mercury at Aries 11 gives 143, less 120, so Leo 23. The chapter carries ONLY the x13 form - no x12 variant appears in it. A second recension follows under the rubric 'Allo ek ton Paulou' with identical arithmetic, which Paulus rates the better of the two because it lets the result fall back in the body's own sign after a full circuit.

paulus_seven_hermetic_lots.location: Eisagogika ch. 23 (κγ΄), Περὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ κλήρων τῶν ἐν τῇ Παναρέτῳ, Boer 1958 pp. 47-51
paulus_seven_hermetic_lots.verified_summary: Each lot is an arc from A to B measured in zodiacal order and projected from the ASCENDANT degree at 30 degrees per sign, and every one carries 'tois de nyktos to anapalin' - the arc reverses by sect. Day arcs: Fortune Sun->Moon; Daimon Moon->Sun; Eros Daimon->Venus; Necessity Mercury->Fortune; Tolma Mars->Fortune; Nike Daimon->Jupiter; Nemesis Saturn->Fortune. Note that Eros and Nike begin from the Lot of Daimon, not from the Ascendant directly. Paulus's rationale pairs each lot with a planet - Moon/Tyche, Sun/Daimon, Venus/Eros, Mercury/Anankē, Mars/Tolma, Jupiter/Nikē, Saturn/Nemesis - with the Ascendant as the basis arbitrating among them. All seven formulas in src/engine/lots.py were checked against this and match.
paulus_seven_hermetic_lots.publication_limit: The source meanings must be printed without replacing severe terms with generic positivity. Each lot is still judged through place, ruler, ruler condition, and configurations. Nemesis does not by itself calculate a death date, and none of these lots authorizes medical, legal, financial, martial, or coercive advice.

paulus_zoidion_monomoiria.location: Eisagogika ch. 5 (ε΄), Boer 1958 p. 18, with the Κανόνιον τῆς μονομοιρίας table at p. 17
paulus_zoidion_monomoiria.verified_summary: One degree per part, thirty parts to a sign. Degree 1 belongs to the DOMICILE LORD of the sign; degree 2 to the next planet in heptazone (Chaldean) order; and so on cyclically to degree 30. A fractional position rounds up - the minutes are counted as a whole degree. The p. 17 table is laid out in seven columns grouped by domicile lord, which confirms the ruler-start.

Boer's apparatus further notes that manuscripts ZY collapse Cancer and Leo into a single series, 'Lunae monomoiriis omissis'. The project's optional +1 score for a planet in its own monomoiria remains a disclosed configured weighting, not a Pauline rule.

paulus_trigonal_monomoiria.location: Eisagogika ch. 32 (λβ΄), Περὶ τῆς κατὰ τρίγωνον μονομοιρίας, Boer 1958 p. 85, table p. 86, apparatus p. 87
paulus_trigonal_monomoiria.verified_summary: The input is the DEGREE OF THE SECT LIGHT, not the sign. The sequence starts from the trigon lord that receives the sect light by sect, and runs in the sect's trigon-lord order rather than the heptazone. One degree per planet, with a strict repeating seven-cycle: no planet takes a second degree before the starting planet has taken its second. The planet holding the sect light's final degree rules. This is what distinguishes it from the zoidion form, which starts from the domicile lord and runs in heptazone order.
paulus_trigonal_monomoiria.publication_limit: THE SOURCE PASSAGE IS EDITORIALLY JUDGED CORRUPT. Boer's apparatus at p. 85,13-15 records Schato's verdict that the passage is 'mutilus et depravatus' and that 'verus sensus inde elici non potuit' - the true sense could not be drawn out of it. Boer reconstructs the constraint from Heliodorus as a control, not from Paulus's own words. Reading the Greek therefore RAISES rather than settles the doubt here: this rule rests on an editor's reconstruction of a mutilated text. It must not be presented to a reader with the same confidence as a clean passage, and a disagreement between implementations is expected rather than anomalous. The prior note that 'manuscript tables varied' understated this.

valens_zodiacal_releasing.location: Chapters 4-7, division from Fortune and Spirit, Loosing of the Bond, and sign period years, pp. 3-14
valens_zodiacal_releasing.verified_summary: Valens releases bodily and circumstantial matters from Fortune, action and reputation from Spirit, describes Loosing of the Bond, and supplies the sign-period years.

al_biruni_firdaria_seven_planet_core.location: Section 395, Firdaria of Planets, printed p. 32 (PDF p. 33)
al_biruni_firdaria_seven_planet_core.verified_summary: For a day nativity the first period begins with the Sun; for a night nativity it begins with the Moon. The remaining planets follow in descending order. Each major period is divided into seven equal parts, beginning with the major chronocrator and continuing with the next planet below.
al_biruni_firdaria_seven_planet_core.publication_limit: Section 395 verifies the seven-planet sequence and equal subperiods. It does not mention the lunar nodes; any node periods must be labeled as a later configured extension, not attributed to this passage.

al_biruni_hayz_halb.location: Section 496, Hayyiz and Halb, printed p. 101 (PDF p. 102)
al_biruni_hayz_halb.verified_summary: Halb matches diurnal planets above ground by day or below at night and nocturnal planets above at night or below by day. Hayyiz adds matching planetary and sign gender; Mars is explicitly male and nocturnal.
al_biruni_hayz_halb.publication_limit: Mercury is conditional on sign or association and remains indeterminate unless that dependency is explicitly modeled. Hayz and halb modify condition; they do not make a malefic benefic or cancel debility.

ptolemy_sect_membership.location: Book I, chapter 7 (ζ΄. Περὶ ἡμερινῶν καὶ νυκτερινῶν), source file lines 2498-2522
ptolemy_sect_membership.verified_summary: Moon and Venus nocturnal; Sun and Jupiter diurnal; Mercury common to both - diurnal when he makes a MORNING appearance, nocturnal when an EVENING one. Saturn, being cooling, is assigned to the heat of the day, and Mars, being drying, to the moisture of the night, 'for thus each, obtaining proportion through the mixture, becomes proper to the sect that provides good temperament.'
ptolemy_sect_membership.publication_limit: Ptolemy's reason for the malefic assignments is TEMPERING by opposite quality, not reward. Mercury's sect is determinate once the solar phase is known - 'common' names the rule, not the answer.

ptolemy_exaltations.location: Book I, chapter 20 (κ΄. Περὶ ὑψωμάτων), source file lines 3904-3977
ptolemy_exaltations.verified_summary: Exaltation and fall by SIGN: Sun Aries/Libra, Moon Taurus/Scorpio, Saturn Libra/Aries, Jupiter Cancer/Capricorn, Mars Capricorn/Cancer, Venus Pisces/Virgo, Mercury Virgo/Pisces. Each is derived from a physical cause - solar declination, the Moon's first phase after conjunction in the Sun's exaltation, and the wind and moisture qualities of the planets.
ptolemy_exaltations.publication_limit: PTOLEMY GIVES NO EXALTATION DEGREES. The chapter assigns exaltations by sign only. The received degrees (Sun 19 Aries and the rest) are a separate and older Egyptian tradition and must be cited to Firmicus or Paulus, never to Ptolemy. Our engine already does this correctly: EXALTATIONS is sign-based and the degree table is cited to hel.firmicus.exaltation_degrees_table.

valens_exaltation_degrees.location: Book III, chapter 4 (Περὶ ἀνέμων τῶν ἀστέρων καὶ τῶν ὑψωμάτων καὶ βαθμῶν), printed p. 140,4
valens_exaltation_degrees.verified_summary: The Sun is exalted about the 19th degree of Aries; the Moon about the 3rd of Taurus; Jupiter about the 15th of Cancer; Mars about the 28th of Capricorn; Saturn about the 21st of Libra; Mercury about the 15th of Virgo; Venus about the 27th of Pisces. All seven verified exact against the engine's EXALTATION table.
valens_exaltation_degrees.publication_limit: PTOLEMY GIVES NO EXALTATION DEGREES - Tetrabiblos I.20 assigns exaltations by SIGN only and derives each from a physical cause. Never cite exaltation degrees to Ptolemy. Valens (c. 165) is roughly 170 years earlier than Firmicus (c. 334) and is now the preferred witness; the Firmicus table remains a valid parallel.

valens_sect_rejoicing_hayz.location: Book III, chapter 5 (Περὶ αἱρέσεως τῶν ἀστέρων), printed p. 141,16
valens_sect_rejoicing_hayz.verified_summary: The Sun, Jupiter and Saturn rejoice being above the earth by day and below by night; the Moon, Mars and Venus rejoice above the earth by night and below by day. Mercury goes according to the sects AND the rulership of the bounds. For day births, one having Jupiter, Sun and Saturn above the earth and well configured is better off than one having them below. Venus rejoices more rising than culminating; the rest rejoice on the Ascendant rather than setting.
valens_sect_rejoicing_hayz.publication_limit: This is the hayz/halb doctrine roughly 860 years before al-Biruni section 496. Two refinements are Valens's own and are NOT in the later transmission: Mercury's sect is taken by sect AND bound rulership (a refinement on Ptolemy I.7's phase rule, not a contradiction), and Venus prefers the Ascendant to the Midheaven while the other planets prefer rising to setting.

valens_lot_of_exaltation.location: Book II, chapter 18 (Περὶ ὑψώματος Ἡλίου καὶ Σελήνης πρὸς εὐδαιμονίαν), printed p. 80,9
valens_lot_of_exaltation.verified_summary: Valens: 'We ourselves also found a certain mystical place from experience: to take, by day, from the natal Sun to ARIES (which is his exaltation), and by night from the Moon to TAURUS, and the same from the Ascendant; and wherever it terminates, look at the place and its lord.' Matches src/engine/lots.py exactly (day Sun->Aries, night Moon->Taurus).
valens_lot_of_exaltation.publication_limit: Not one of the seven Hermetic lots of Paulus ch. 23. Valens presents it as his own discovery from experience, so it carries his authority alone and should be labelled as such.

valens_lord_of_year_naming_hazard.location: Book I, chapter 11 (printed p. 27,1) contrasted with Book IV, chapter 11 (printed p. 174)
valens_lord_of_year_naming_hazard.verified_summary: Valens carries TWO distinct techniques under the phrase 'lord of the year'. I.11 is a CALENDRICAL reckoning: take the years since Augustus plus intercalary days plus days from Thoth to the birthday, subtract sevens, and count the remainder from the Sun. IV.11 is the ANNUAL PROFECTION: divide the age by twelve and let the remainder count the sign. The engine implements the profection.
valens_lord_of_year_naming_hazard.publication_limit: Do not conflate them. Valens himself rejects the universal form of the calendrical one: 'that those born in the same year should have obtained one and the same rulership does not seem to have reason.' He prefers an epoch taken from the heliacal rising of Sirius over the civil new year.

valens_bound_delineations.location: Book I, chapter 3 (Περὶ ὁρίων), printed pp. 14-19
valens_bound_delineations.verified_summary: Valens delineates each of the sixty Egyptian bounds individually. The degree boundaries were checked digit by digit against EGYPTIAN_TERMS in all twelve signs; Libra is a manuscript outlier Kroll flags at 16,18. All 60 delineations were read directly from the Greek and rendered into English in docs/sources/valens_translation.md. The chapter closes (p. 19,4-7) by stating that the degrees were set out ALONE for teaching, and that with the domicile lord lying upon them it accomplishes its own, either base or good.
valens_bound_delineations.publication_limit: A delineation of the DEGREES, not a verdict on the person. Never publish a bound line as a free-standing judgment: the overlying domicile lord decides whether what the degree carries comes out base or good, and placement and sect outweigh the bound. Valens attaches conditions constantly and they reverse outcomes - Sagittarius in Mercury bound gives philosophers when Mercury inclines and soldiers when Mars; Capricorn in Jupiter bound produces BOTH reputation and disrepute.

valens_causative_place.verified_summary: A Lot built from Saturn and Mars alone (day: Saturn->Mars from Asc; night: Mars->Saturn), which Valens states governs fears, dangers, and confinement when a malefic owns or aspects it.
valens_causative_place.publication_limit: Reports the place and whether a malefic owns its sign; does not assert activation without that testimony.

valens_syzygy_climacteric.verified_summary: Profect one sign per year from the ascendant; a year whose profected sign is the pre-natal syzygy sign, or its square or opposition, is climacteric and disturbed, especially with transiting Saturn in a cadent place.
valens_syzygy_climacteric.publication_limit: Lists the years the rule marks. Names no event and grades no severity beyond the aggravating Saturn witness Valens himself gives.

lilly_manners_significator_cascade.location: Book III, Chap. CVII (significator selection, printed pp. 534-539) and Chap. CVIII (planet-by-planet table, pp. 539-542)
lilly_manners_significator_cascade.verified_summary: The significator of manners is any planet occupying the ascending sign; failing that, the planet joined to the Moon or Mercury; failing that, the Lord of the ascendant provided his dispositor beholds him with aspect; failing that, the planet in partile aspect to Moon or Mercury; failing that, whichever planet holds most essential dignity in the places of Moon and Mercury. Chapter CVIII then gives each planet two states, well-dignified and ill-dignified, with distinct character lists (no Sun/Moon rows; the lights only modify via combustion, increasing light, or latitude). Mercury unfortunate and in an airy sign square or opposite the Moon or Venus reads as deceitful and destructive; Mercury well-dignified reads as sharp-fancied, studious, capable of learning without a teacher. Worst manners come from the infortunes joined to each other or to Mercury in the 7th, 8th, or 9th.
lilly_manners_significator_cascade.publication_limit: This is a delineation technique for temperament, not an event prediction; publish freely once the significator selection is shown, but state which branch (well/ill dignified) fired and why.

lilly_wit_and_understanding.location: Book III, Chap. CIX, printed pp. 543-545/538
lilly_wit_and_understanding.verified_summary: Wit is read from Mercury and the Moon jointly: Mercury governs the rational soul, the Moon the vegetative/sensory brain. Base rule: their places well affected and mutually aspecting each other by a good aspect gives excellent wit; no aspect at all, or a hard aspect, gives dull capacity. Independently, Mercury's own condition modifies this: angular, in his own house, swift, oriental, unafflicted by Mars, gives sharp and self-taught understanding regardless of the Moon link. Corrupt wit requires Mercury peregrine AND cadent AND combust AND slow AND afflicted by the infortunes together, not any one alone.
lilly_wit_and_understanding.publication_limit: Two rules in this chapter can point opposite directions on the same chart (the Mercury-Moon aspect test versus Mercury's own-condition tests). When they disagree, publish both branches and say so; do not silently pick the more flattering one.

lilly_stature_form_and_grossness.location: Book III, Chap. CX (stature, leaf printed 538), the unnumbered proportion-of-members section (pp. 538-539), Chap. CXI (nature of signs, colour of face/hair, pp. 539-548), and Chap. CXII (grossness/leanness, leaf printed 549/542)
lilly_stature_form_and_grossness.verified_summary: Physical description is read from whichever planet partilely beholds the Lord of the ascendant, with a stated per-planet stature table split by oriental/occidental, modified by the sign that planet or the ascending sign occupies. Grossness/leanness is read from the sign ascending and its Lord, changing partway through the sign (a stated first-half/second-half split per sign).
lilly_stature_form_and_grossness.publication_limit: Project-internal testing against two real photographs of one native scored two hits, two misses, and one confound, at a sample size of one. This branch of the tradition should be treated as unvalidated for physical description; do not publish physical appearance claims from this technique as confident fact. Keep it available for research use only, per the unverified_handling policy.

lilly_general_fortune_and_riches.location: Book III, Chap. CXIII (general fortune/misery, pp. 543/552), the unnumbered second-house riches section (pp. 552-553), Chap. CXIIII (whether rich, pp. 553-554), Chap. CXV (means of estate, pp. 554-561), Chap. CXVI (just or indirect means, pp. 560-562), Chap. CXVII (durability of estate, pp. 562-564)
lilly_general_fortune_and_riches.verified_summary: General fortune: three or four planets essentially dignified, or receiving one another from dignity, gives ample fortune; most planets in fall/detriment/abject houses/peregrine gives many infelicities; a genuine mixture of both (some strong, some weak, or well-fortified planets in miserable houses) gives Lilly's own named outcome, unequal and variable fortune across a life, which does not reduce to a single good/bad verdict. Riches: significators are the 2nd cusp and its Lord, any planet intercepted in the 2nd, the Part of Fortune and its Lord, and Jupiter generally; strength and house placement of these, by plurality of testimony, gives poverty, sufficiency, or wealth, with source of wealth read from the ruling planet's natural significations and the house it occupies.
lilly_general_fortune_and_riches.publication_limit: When the mixed-testimony condition fires (roughly equal counts of strong and weak significators), publish the 'unequal fortune, splendid in parts, dejected in others' verdict rather than forcing a single good-or-bad rating; this is Lilly's own named outcome, not a hedge invented downstream.

lilly_sixth_house_health.location: Book III: 'Of the Infirmities and Diseases of Bodyes' (pp. 576-581), 'Of the Tooth-ach' (p. 583), 'Of the Falling-sicknesse and Madnesse' (pp. 583-584), 'Of the Stone' (pp. 584-585), Chap. CXXIX 'Whether the Disease...be curable or not' (pp. 585-586)
lilly_sixth_house_health.verified_summary: Five significators: ascending sign and Lord, Sun and Moon (Moon for humours, Sun for vital spirit), 6th house and its Lord, planet(s) in the 6th, 7th house and its Lord. A significator afflicted BOTH by its own weakness AND by a hostile aspect from a malefic gives a more vehement affliction; weak alone or aspected alone (not both) gives a milder one. The falling-sickness/madness chapter states four causes that concur together (Mercury and Moon in aversion; both in evil cadent houses without aspecting the ascendant; the out-of-sect malefic strong and angular afflicting both; Saturn/Mars dispositing both) -- it explicitly frames these as a converging set, not independent triggers, and provides no benefic-rescue clause anywhere in that specific chapter. Curability (adjacent chapter CXXIX) requires benefics in trine/sextile to the disease significators AND those significators in movable signs for an easy cure; essential dignity of the disease-significator itself defeats an otherwise-promised cure.
lilly_sixth_house_health.publication_limit: The falling-sickness/madness register (epilepsy, mania) is a severe clinical claim from a 17th-century source with no modern validation and no stated benefic rescue. Do not publish this delineation to a customer from a partial trigger (e.g., the aversion condition alone, which occurs in roughly one chart in three by unrelated project testing); require the full stated concurrence of causes before including it, and even then flag it as unvalidated historical doctrine, not a diagnosis.

lilly_marriage_men_and_wife_description.location: Book III, 'Of Marriage: and first of Mens Marriages' through the number-of-wives and mutual-love chapters, printed pp. approximately 543-563 (djvu line 52324 onward)
lilly_marriage_men_and_wife_description.verified_summary: Significators of a wife: the 7th house and its Lord, and any planet posited in the 7th. Whether the native marries is read from the Moon and Venus (fruitful/legitimate marriage) versus Saturn (monkery/single life), by strength, sign barrenness, and house. The physical form and shape of the wife is explicitly cross-referenced by Lilly to the general planet-and-sign body-description material (Chap. CX/CXI), applied to the 7th Lord; the wife's temperament is read via Ptolemy's method as Lilly transmits it, from whichever of Saturn/Jupiter/Mars/Venus/Mercury (Sun and Moon excluded) the Moon makes her very first applying aspect to after the moment of birth, graded by that planet's own condition (well or ill placed).
lilly_marriage_men_and_wife_description.publication_limit: The Moon's first post-natal application must be computed by real ephemeris stepping, not approximated from a rounded birth time; a near-tie between two candidate planets (observed at under two hours' difference in one project test case) should be reported as a near-tie, with both readings given, not collapsed to the nominal winner.

lilly_children_precedence_and_testimonie.location: Book III, 'The fift House...Of Children,' unnumbered section pp. 602-604, and Chap. CXXXVIII 'How many Children,' pp. 604-606
lilly_children_precedence_and_testimonie.verified_summary: Significators, in order: the 5th house, then the 11th, then the 1st. Fruitful planets are Jupiter, Venus, Moon (and the Head, by extension); barren are Saturn, Mars, Sun (and the Tail); Mercury is indifferent and follows whatever planet it conjoins or whose dignity it occupies. A fruitful planet in a barren sign is explicitly named mediocrity, requiring recourse to the other significator houses rather than a direct verdict. The chapter's own strongest stated negative testimony is the Lord of the 5th retrograde, especially if he is an infortune -- called outright 'the greatest argument of having no children' -- yet Lilly attaches his own counter-example caveat to that exact rule, describing a nativity where it did not hold despite the couple being, in his words, 'very likely people.'
lilly_children_precedence_and_testimonie.publication_limit: When the raw count of testimonies and the chapter's own named strongest single testimony point in opposite directions, publish both and note the conflict; do not resolve it by simple majority count, since Lilly's own worked caveat warns specifically against over-trusting this exact rule.

lilly_profession_significator_cascade.location: Book III, Chap. CXLVIII 'Of the Magistery, Exercitation or Profession of the Native,' printed p. 624-626, and Chap. CXLIX, pp. 626-634
lilly_profession_significator_cascade.verified_summary: The significator of profession is selected from exactly three candidate planets -- Mars, Venus, Mercury -- through five ordered fallback rules, each used only if the previous fails: (1) a candidate in the 10th/1st/7th, in its own essential dignity, clear of the Sun; (2) a candidate that is Lord of the sign on the Midheaven and essentially dignified; (3) a candidate in a partile aspect to the Moon, tie-broken by strength, best aspect, tightest orb, then sinister before dexter; (4) a candidate aspecting the Moon within her orb with a powerful, unafflicted aspect; (5) last resort, whichever of the three next rises before the Sun. Natives resolved only by rules 3-5 typically handle an ignoble trade or none at all. A significator in strong, good aspect to a second candidate can relinquish its claim, and the native follows the second planet's trade signification instead (strength of the mixing aspect, and applying versus separating, should temper how completely the claim transfers). Success (fame, excellence) requires the significator dignified, unafflicted by partile malefic configuration, angular, AND oriental -- all four; missing orientality alone caps the outcome at solid competence rather than renown.
lilly_profession_significator_cascade.publication_limit: Report the exact rule number (1 through 5) that resolved the significator, since Lilly himself says natives resolved late in the cascade tend toward disreputable or absent trades -- that context changes how the resulting delineation should read.

lilly_friends_and_enemies_11th_12th.location: Book III, unnumbered 11th-house chapter 'Of Friends' (printed p. 634) and Chap. CL 'Quality of Friends' (p. 636); unnumbered 12th-house chapter 'Of Enemies' (p. 639) through Chap. CLV 'Of Captivity or Imprisonment' (pp. 642-643)
lilly_friends_and_enemies_11th_12th.verified_summary: Friends are read first from planets in or aspecting the 11th, then from planets in the 1st, then from the Lord of the 11th. An infortune with no essential dignity in a movable or common sign in the 11th is named explicitly as the worst signification of false friends Lilly says he has found in his own practice. Enemies are read from planets in the 7th or 12th and from the Lord of the 12th; the Lord of the 12th failing to behold the Lord of the ascendant is a stated argument for comparatively few enemies, and the Lord of the 12th placed IN the ascendant is a stated rescue turning likely enemies into friends.
lilly_friends_and_enemies_11th_12th.publication_limit: None beyond the general policy; this material tested as internally consistent (four independent rules converging on a single chart in project testing).

lilly_violent_death_arguments.location: Book III, Chap. CLVI 'Of Death, whether Violent or Naturall,' printed pp. 644-650
lilly_violent_death_arguments.verified_summary: Fifteen distinct, mostly compound arguments for a violent death are given, each requiring several named conditions together (sign of the Lights, affliction by a specific malefic, angularity, fixed-star proximity, etc). A general exception is stated to override every one of the fifteen: one Fortune in the ascendant and the other in the 8th removes all fear of sudden or violent death regardless of any other testimony present. Lilly gives no fixed count of testimonies required, only a confidence scale (more concurring testimonies warrant more confidence), and states plainly that a malefic must be angular for real certainty, with the aphorisms otherwise not operating on their own without a serious mixture of judgment. Absent every one of the fifteen arguments, the default judgment is a natural death by sickness, with quality read from the planet and sign in the 8th.
lilly_violent_death_arguments.publication_limit: This chapter concerns a topic your own project has already excluded from customer-facing reports (length-of-life/manner-of-death techniques were removed after failing on 11 of 20 known test cases). Do not publish violent-death delineation to customers under any branch of this rule; keep it internal-only per the unverified_handling policy, and never report a single non-angular, isolated testimony as meaningful even for internal research.

lilly_directions_measure_of_time.location: Book III, Chap. CLVII (duration of effects, pp. 654-656), Chap. CLVIII (five hylegiacal places, p. 656), and the chapter 'Of the measure of time in Directions,' printed pp. 708-715
lilly_directions_measure_of_time.verified_summary: Lilly names three competing arc-to-time keys and states an explicit preference order: Ptolemy's simple 1 degree of the equator = 1 year (used when time is short); Maginus's variable solar-arc-in-right-ascension method (a full annual table, sampled and internally consistent, though Lilly's own two worked examples using it contain arithmetic errors); and Naibod's method, which Lilly calls in his own words 'the most exactest measure that hitherto hath been found out' and uses whenever he has sufficient time to do a nativity properly. Naibod's table implies a constant rate of 0 degrees 59 minutes 8 seconds of arc per year (0.9856 degrees/year) -- this numeric constant does not appear as a stated single figure in Lilly's text, it is derived from his printed year/day/hour table and independently matches the constant already in use in this project's own primary-directions module. No orb-of-time (how long before/after the exact hit effects begin to show) is given anywhere in this material despite Chap. CLVII's title suggesting one; that chapter is entirely about the relative strength of effects, not their timing window. No converse (reverse-motion) directions are given anywhere in this range -- Lilly's method as printed is direct-motion only.
lilly_directions_measure_of_time.publication_limit: Default the engine's direction calculations to the Naibod key (0.9856 deg/year) rather than the simpler Ptolemaic key, since that is Lilly's own stated first choice; retain Ptolemy's key as an available fallback/comparison mode, consistent with how Lilly himself used it. Do not implement converse directions and attribute them to Lilly; that would misrepresent the source.

lilly_profections_lord_of_year_and_revol.location: Book III, Chap. CLXVI 'Of annuall Profections' (pp. 715-718), Chap. CLXVII 'Of the Use of Profections' (pp. 718-726), Chap. CLXVIII 'How to judge upon a Figure of Profections' (pp. 726-728), Chaps. CLXIX-CLXXI (profections of Asc/Moon, MC/Sun, Part of Fortune/2nd, pp. 729-734), Chap. CLXXII 'Of Revolutions' (pp. 734-737), Chap. CLXXIII 'Of the Returne of the Planets' (pp. 738-741)
lilly_profections_lord_of_year_and_revol.verified_summary: Annual profection moves every house cusp one whole sign per solar year, keeping the radical degree and minute fixed, beginning at the solar return; Lilly explicitly abandons monthly (13 divisions/year) and daily sub-profections as impractical in his own practice, despite stating their rates. The Lord of the Year is the Lord of the profected ascending sign; when the profected ascendant sits away from the very start of its sign, TWO lords split the year proportionally by degrees remaining, using the same degree-to-time key as directions (12 days 4 hours 12 minutes per degree at the profectional scale). Profections alone are stated to 'effect little' -- they time and amplify or dampen a direction's effects, they do not substitute for one. The Lord of the Year is judged by comparing his condition in the radix against his condition in the solar-return (revolution) chart for the same year; a 'good year' requires him direct in BOTH figures among other conditions, so a natally retrograde Lord of the Year cannot achieve the chapter's top verdict regardless of how well-placed the revolution shows him. Revolutions are cast to the exact minute of solar return and compared cusp-by-cusp and lord-by-lord against the radix; radical significators act that year through whatever house of the revolution they fall into.
lilly_profections_lord_of_year_and_revol.publication_limit: Report the Lord-of-Year determination together with its radix condition explicitly; a retrograde-natally Lord of the Year should never be reported as achieving the chapter's best-case verdict even if strongly placed by the revolution alone.

lilly_rectification_animodar_trutine_acc.location: Book III, Chap. XCVIII 'Trutine of Hermes' (pp. 501-505), Chap. XCIX 'Rectification by Animodar' (pp. 505-506), Chap. C 'Rectification by Accidents' (pp. 507-519)
lilly_rectification_animodar_trutine_acc.verified_summary: Three rectification methods, in Lilly's own stated order of trust, least to most: the Trutine of Hermes (Moon's place at conception should equal the Ascendant at birth, via a lunar-mansion-in-womb table) -- Lilly says it will rarely hold to better than two or three degrees and gives it help only to the sign, rarely the exact degree; Animodar (the planet with most essential dignity at the preceding new/full Moon's degree sets the Ascendant or MC to its own degree) -- Lilly states outright that neither of these first two methods is as sound as rectification by accidents; rectification by accidents, which directs the Ascendant (for bodily/health events) and the Midheaven (for honour/preferment/marriage events) to their promittors and adjusts the birth angles until the arc-to-time distance matches the native's own remembered, dated past life events. Lilly explicitly rejects rectifying by transits or by a profection figure alone, citing his own failure to find either reliable in practice.
lilly_rectification_animodar_trutine_acc.publication_limit: Rectification by accidents requires the native's own dated life events as input; it cannot be run or simulated from chart data alone. Do not present a rectified Ascendant/MC to a customer without real input events, and always report the pre-rectification chart's technique-dependent findings as provisional until (or unless) rectification is actually performed.

lilly_worked_nativity_method_notes.location: Book III, 'The Nativity of an English Merchant Astrologically handled,' printed pp. 742-764
lilly_worked_nativity_method_notes.verified_summary: Lilly's own worked demonstration diverges from his stated doctrine in several traceable ways: he reverse-engineers sibling-count testimonies to match a known biographical fact (seven siblings) after his own stated method predicts few, without flagging the fit as post-hoc; he overrides Ptolemy's own stated exclusion of the Sun from being Anareta when no other candidate is convenient, explicitly reasoning his way around the exclusion; he treats a partile square in signs of long ascension as equivalent in force to a trine via ascensional-difference reasoning not set up anywhere in his doctrinal chapters; and one of his own predictions (no throat blemish) is corrected by the book's own marginal annotation, which states the native did in fact have a defect Lilly's method missed. Conversely, several of his practices validate cautious method: he requires convergence of several testimonies before committing to grave claims and states explicitly that one testimony for a violent death is not enough on its own; he treats the absence of any firing rule as valid evidence for the negative (no imprisonment, because none of his own aphorisms fired); and he never computes a hyleg/length-of-life figure anywhere in the actual working, deferring timing of death entirely to directions and declining to give an age.
lilly_worked_nativity_method_notes.publication_limit: Treat Lilly's own worked example as evidence that the tradition's founder was not immune to retrofitting known outcomes onto ambiguous rule sets; this is a caution for how the whole corpus should be read, not a license to do the same. Use his good practices (require convergence, treat rule-silence as evidence, defer length-of-life) as house style; do not import his single instance of retrofitting as a technique.
